_readme: Content-hash pins for files whose HEADER ASSERTS THE BODY HAS NOT CHANGED since it landed. A vendoring header is an assertion about the day the file landed; it cannot see later edits, so an audit-scope exclusion resting on 'it is vendored' depends on something nobody re-checks. script/v2/check-vendored-pins.sh fails when a pinned file's sha256 differs from its entry here, and names the file. T-574. WHICH FILES ARE PINNED IS DECIDED BY READING EACH HEADER, NOT BY DIRECTORY -- see notPinned below, which records the ones deliberately left out so the next reader does not re-litigate them. TO CHANGE A PINNED FILE ON PURPOSE: update the sha256 here in the SAME commit, and say in the message why the body moved.
algorithm: sha256 of the file bytes, as printed by shasum -a 256 (or sha256sum)

pinned.assertion: Apart from these comment lines and the two forgefmt markers, every line is identical to that file, in order. Do not edit or reformat it; diff it against the URL instead.
pinned.why: The audit scope excludes it as vendored. That exclusion is only sound while the body is unchanged.

pinned.assertion: This file is a verbatim copy of src/interfaces/IValoremClear.sol from the Blockscout-verified source ... Comments only have changed from the verified copy. If Valorem's deployment ever moves, re-transcribe rather than adapt.
pinned.upstream: Blockscout-verified source of Overcall's NVDA registry on chain 4663 (0x8E973cE1A6884E28Ad3E377d5f670Bc0b463f4EA); hand transcription of valorem-labs-inc/clear @ 6436c823f560af493af119d6148fb3237037aca4
pinned.why: Its header says re-transcribe rather than adapt, which is a fixedness claim about the body. It is NOT byte-identical to any upstream file -- the provenance paragraph itself differs -- so the pin is against its own recorded bytes, not against Valorem.

pinned.assertion: MIRRORED, NOT RE-DERIVED. Copied line for line from the v4-core checkout on this machine. If v4-core changes these, this file is wrong and the pin must be re-mirrored from the same path.
pinned.upstream: Uniswap v4-core src/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:8,17-23; local checkout recorded by the file header
pinned.why: This test-only dependency mirror is deliberately independent of the production decode sites. Silent edits would make the supposed upstream reference agree with the code under test for the wrong reason.

notPinned.why: NOT VENDORED. Its own header says it is a REWRITE with its own TickOutOfRange error, a uint256[20] factor table instead of the unrolled chain, and no getTickAtSqrtRatio. T-529 established this. Pinning it would assert a fixedness its header explicitly denies, and would freeze first-party code on the price path.
notPinned.note: src/v2/README.md:40 still lists it beside FullMath.sol as 'Vendored unchanged from Uniswap v3-core' -- that line contradicts the file's own header and is out of this row's scope to fix. Reported, not repaired.

notPinned.why: Checked, per this row's criterion 3. It carries no vendoring header. It copies Policy.normalizeSpot's arithmetic from v1 and its own @dev states a DELIBERATE divergence -- it reports ok = false where normalizeSpot reverted -- so it is first-party code that was written from a model, not a copy held fixed.

Hand-written interfaces. Their claim is ABI-compatibility with v4-core and SwapRouter02 ('ABI-identical', 'encodes to the same five static words'), which is a statement about the encoding, not about the bytes of an upstream file. A content pin would not test that claim; a selector or pool-id assertion would.
